tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. - (idea by coach) Constraint: fvm-pinned Flutter and Dart version is real, turn it into an asset by committing .fvmrc in F000 day one so no later unit can silently drift
- (idea by coach) Constraint: flutter_bloc only is real, asset is one base Cubit or Bloc helper in core defining the same loading-data-error shape so nine feature blocs do not reinvent it
- (idea by coach) Constraint: Clean Architecture layering is real but the safety is imagined until enforced, add an import-linter rule in F000 rather than relying on a human promise
- (idea by coach) Constraint: fpdart Either everywhere is real, asset is one Failure hierarchy in core, built once in F000, mapped from the 13 backend error codes, that every feature data layer reuses
- (idea by coach) Constraint: mocktail for test doubles is real, asset is one fake HTTP client and fake clock pattern shipped from F000 that every later unit copies for the RNF07 80 percent target
- (idea by coach) Constraint: whisper_ggml on-device speech-to-text belongs to RF02, but F000 should still decide where the native plugin or isolate boundary lives so RF02 does not invent app-wide threading alone
- (idea by coach) Constraint: design_tokens.dart as single visual source is real, asset is generating it mechanically from prototype-extract.md section 3 instead of hand-transcribing, removing a whole class of RNF08 drift bugs
- (idea by coach) Constraint: iOS portrait only actually removes work, no orientation handling, no tablet layouts, no Android shims, resist building for future portability nobody asked for
- (idea by coach) Constraint: the fixed 5 minute background session timeout is simplest as one AppLifecycleState listener plus a timestamp in the auth-vault shell, not duplicated per screen
- (idea by coach) Constraint: the device-only biometric or PIN vault has zero network failure modes to design for, only local_auth or PIN failure states, which is genuinely freeing
- (idea by coach) Challenge an imagined constraint: a frozen backend contract does not forbid a generated HTTP client, but codegen is still not worth it for roughly 25 endpoints on a solo timeline
- (idea by coach) Challenge an imagined constraint: three layers per feature does not mean three mandatory files, a thin presentation layer can be one file when a screen is simple, like the RF09 dashboard
- (idea by coach) Leverage point: of the fixed constraints, only the Failure hierarchy and the base bloc state shape are genuinely cross-feature infrastructure F000 must build directly
- (idea by coach) Constraint: RNF09 needs 5 write endpoints times 3 failure types, 15 countable scenarios, F000 can pre-build one parametrized test harness so later units fill a table instead of writing 15 tests from scratch
- (idea by coach) Constraint: RLS is enforced entirely server-side, so the client HTTP layer only needs to always attach the bearer token, simpler than it first looks
- (idea by coach) Constraint: Supabase is the only backend, route around pulling in the full supabase_flutter package by treating Supabase purely as a dio base URL per the x-cerne-function convention, since auth and biometrics are handled separately
- (idea by coach) Constraint: the apikey and Authorization header rules are easy to get wrong by hand each call, dissolve the risk by building the rule entirely into one dio interceptor so no feature code ever sets headers itself
- (idea by coach) Constraint: audio must never leave the device, establish the whisper_ggml isolate or plugin boundary early so RF02 is not the first unit discovering threading problems
- (idea by coach) Reframe: a frozen backend is a gift for a solo project, no backend bugs to chase and no API renegotiation, F000 can be built entirely against the OpenAPI contract and fixtures
- (idea by coach) Reframe: the free-choices section is not freedom, it is risk ownership, whichever library F000 picks becomes load-bearing for nine more units with no external veto to catch a bad pick
- (idea by coach) Constraint: fvm is pinned per repository not per machine, F000 should fill the Running and verifying TODO in AGENTS.md with the exact fvm command sequence the moment the project scaffolds
- (technique by coach) started SCAMPER Method
- (idea by coach) Substitute: replace hand-written DTO and JSON mapping with freezed plus json_serializable codegen for Entry, ChatMessage and ExportJob
- (idea by coach) Substitute: replace per-feature loading-error-data state classes with one generic Resource sealed class shared from core
- (idea by coach) Substitute: replace a hand-rolled debounce Timer in RF06 with one reusable Debouncer utility in core used by any future debounced input
- (idea by coach) Combine: merge the HTTP client and the offline-cache read path behind one repository-facing helper that decides network versus cache, so features never choose that themselves
- (idea by coach) Combine: pair design_tokens.dart generation with a golden-screenshot test step so RNF08 visual fidelity is partly machine-checked, not just promised
- (idea by coach) Combine: merge the auth vault and session-refresh logic into one AppStartupGate that owns both, since RF03 and RF07 both hinge on the same expiry clock
- (idea by coach) Combine: drive the vault background timeout and the HTTP token-refresh timing from one shared app-lifecycle clock instead of two independent timers that could drift
- (idea by coach) Adapt: turn the closed 13-code backend error taxonomy into a generated Dart enum so Failure mapping switches over a closed set the compiler can exhaustiveness-check
- (idea by coach) Adapt: treat every screens multiple visible states, RF02 four states and RF04 three states, as instances of one generic view-state enum rather than nine bespoke ones
- (idea by coach) Magnify: invest more than F000 strictly needs in the fake-clock and fake-http test harness, since the RNF07 80 percent target multiplies across nine more units
- (idea by coach) Shrink: scope F000 navigation to exactly the skeleton the flowchart needs, splash to vault to home to side menu, nothing speculative beyond it
- (idea by coach) Put to other use: have the design-token generator also emit a ThemeData object, not just raw constants, so widgets read Theme.of(context) with less import noise while staying single-sourced
- (idea by coach) Put to other use: reuse the dio retry interceptor backoff policy for the RF05 export-job status polling instead of writing a separate poller
- (idea by coach) Eliminate: no home-grown JWT parsing, hold Supabase tokens as opaque and let auth/refresh and auth/session be the only source of truth for validity
- (idea by coach) Eliminate: no speculative future-platform abstractions, Android channel shims or tablet breakpoints, since iOS portrait only already forbids needing them
- (idea by coach) Eliminate: no shared god repository interface, keep each feature repository interface in its own domain layer per RNF06 even though centralizing looks tempting in F000
- (idea by coach) Eliminate: no generic BaseRepository with shared CRUD methods, independent repositories per feature with no shared base that could tempt cross-imports
- (idea by coach) Reverse: write the Failure hierarchy and the 15-scenario RNF09 harness before the first real HTTP call is wired, so every repository is built test-first against a known contract
- (idea by coach) Reverse: let the router itself redirect on a single AuthStatus stream via a redirect callback, so screens stay dumb instead of each screen checking auth state on build
- (idea by coach) Reverse: shape the shared save-use-case interface that RF10 needs in F000 before RF04 or RF01 exist, so RNF06 is satisfied by construction rather than retrofitted later
- (technique by coach) started First Principles Thinking
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: every repository must return Either Failure T, so the Failure shape should mirror the backend error shape plus exactly one local-only variant for failures that never touch the network
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: retryable is a server-asserted flag, so the try-again button logic should render purely on retryable being true, never on client-side guessing from error codes
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: session state is binary, valid or expired, so F000 needs exactly one SessionStatus stream that every bloc subscribes to, nothing else independently decides login state
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: the vault is 100 percent local, so rebuild it with no async Either plumbing at all, threading a synchronous local decision through the same Either as network calls would be over-engineering
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: entries are immutable with no PATCH or DELETE, so the entries repository interface should never expose update or delete methods, not even as unimplemented stubs
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: offline allows only viewing cached data, never writing, so write methods like createEntry and sendMessage should have no offline code path at all, no optimistic queueing to reconcile later
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: RF08 and RF10 are explicitly described as sharing the same failure-isolation pattern, that repetition in the spec is permission to build one isolatedSideEffect helper used by both instead of two parallel implementations
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: PII check and embedding happen inside POST /entries, so the client needs no PII-awareness logic at all, resist adding client-side pre-filtering for safety
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: the spec explicitly states no risk-signal detection as a scope decision, so F000 should not add defensive risk-detection hooks just in case, that door is deliberately closed
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: design_tokens.dart is the single source with zero hardcoded values allowed, rebuilding from scratch means no screen widget holds even one temporary literal color or number
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: no BLoC imports another BLoC directly is stated for RF07 but is really a whole-app pattern, cross-feature communication should be repository or stream level everywhere, not just in the timeline screen
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: chat messages never become entries automatically except the explicit RF10 action, so chat and entries should be modeled as genuinely separate aggregates in the folder structure, resisting a shared Record supertype
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: the background session timeout is fixed and explicitly not configurable, so it belongs as a hardcoded Duration constant in core, never exposed through Settings even as a hidden toggle
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: whisper_ggml never sends audio to the backend, so the RF02 domain use case should take raw audio in and text out with zero awareness of where transcription runs, keeping the constraint enforced by architecture not convention
- (idea by coach) Bedrock fact: the 13 backend error codes are a closed set, so the Failure-mapping function should switch over the enum with no default case, making a hypothetical 14th code a compile error instead of a silent runtime gap
- (insight by coach) Two of the free choices, secure storage and biometrics, are really one decision, the vault, not two independent parameters, worth collapsing in any eventual decision matrix
- (insight by coach) The shared failure-isolation wording for RF08 and RF10 reads as a spec-level hint toward one shared helper, not a coincidence of similar phrasing
- (insight by coach) F000 real deliverable is not picking seven libraries, it is building the two or three shared abstractions, Failure hierarchy, view-state shape, and auth-session gate, that make every later RF unit boring to implement
- (question by coach) Should F000 also decide the test-fixture strategy for shaping fake HTTP responses, given RNF09 needs 15 scenarios across only 5 write endpoints, or should that be deferred to each RF unit
- (question by coach) Is a relational cache like drift overkill if RF06 filters, source plus date range with AND logic, could be satisfied by simple in-memory predicates over a Hive-cached list, does the query complexity actually justify SQL
- (technique by coach) started Reverse Brainstorming
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: pick a chart package with a heavy native dependency early, so every later build and CI run slows down for all nine units, not just RF09 -> invert: prefer pure-Dart packages in F000 whenever a pure-Dart option meets the acceptance criteria
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: let the HTTP client silently swallow the retryable flag and hardcode retry logic per feature -> invert: the interceptor is the single place retry policy lives, features never re-derive it
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: build the Failure hierarchy as one giant catch-all GenericFailure class -> invert: keep it a closed sealed hierarchy mirroring the 13 backend codes plus the one local-only variant, so pattern matching stays exhaustive
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: skip the import-linter rule in F000 and promise to check RNF06 by hand later -> invert: wire the lint rule before the second feature folder exists, not after a violation is found
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: let two different features each invent their own loading-error-data state enum with slightly different names -> invert: the shared view-state shape ships from core before RF01 starts
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: wire biometrics and secure storage as two independent, uncoordinated pieces so a biometric failure can leave the PIN fallback in an inconsistent state -> invert: one vault service owns both paths behind a single state machine
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: generate design_tokens.dart once by hand from the prototype and never revisit it as the prototype extract gets corrected -> invert: make token generation a repeatable script, not a one-time manual transcription
- (idea by coach) Sabotage: let the session-expiry stream be derived independently in three different places, auth vault, router, and HTTP interceptor -> invert: one SessionStatus source of truth, the other two merely subscribe

- (idea by coach) Sabotage: choose a DI package requiring heavy codegen, then let the build_runner step become so slow that later units avoid regenerating it and drift out of sync -> invert: pick the DI approach whose feedback loop stays fast enough that nobody is tempted to skip it

- (idea by coach) Sabotage: let the PIN fallback store the PIN in plaintext in shared_preferences because secure storage felt like overkill for a 4-digit code -> invert: the vault always uses the platform secure store for the PIN hash and biometrics alike, no plaintext exception

- (insight by coach) Synthesis: four techniques (constraint mapping, SCAMPER-reverse, first principles, reverse brainstorming) independently converge on a second decision: the Failure hierarchy plus a parametrized fake-HTTP test harness is F000 deliverable number one, built before any repository, not retrofitted after RF04

content.content:
1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |

| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |

| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |

---

## 7. Integrated flowchart — screens × requirements × backend

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph T0["Screen 0 — Splash"]
        direction TB
        E01["GET /auth/session"]
    end

    subgraph T01["Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault · RF03"]
        direction TB
        E02b["Face ID / Touch ID / PIN — validated on the device, no backend call"]
        E02["POST /auth/login (if the session has fully expired)"]
    end

    subgraph T1["Screen 1 — Home (chat) · RF04, RF08, RF10"]
        direction TB
        E04["POST /chat/sessions"]
        E05["GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06["POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages"]
        E06b["POST .../messages/:userMessageId/retry"]
        E07["POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight"]
        E07b["POST /entries (save message)"]
    end

    subgraph T2["Screen 2 — Insertion modal · RF01, RF02"]
        direction TB
        E08["POST /media/ocr"]
        E09["POST /entries"]
    end

    subgraph T3["Screen 3 — Side menu"]
        direction TB
        E10["GET /chat/sessions"]
        E10b["'Novo Chat' button — opens T1 empty, backed by E04"]
    end

    subgraph T4["Screen 4 — My records · RF05, RF06, RF07"]
        direction TB
        E11["GET /entries (source/dateFrom/dateTo — no category)"]
        E12["GET /entries/search"]
        E15["POST /export/summary"]
        E15b["GET /export/:jobId/status"]
        E16["GET /export/:jobId/download"]
    end

    subgraph T5["Screen 5 — Action plans (extension)"]
        direction TB
        E17["No calls — static"]
    end

    subgraph T6["Screen 6 — Settings · RF09, RNF05"]
        direction TB
        E18["GET /dashboard/aggregate"]

    end

    T0 --> T01 --> T1

    T3 --> T4
    T3 --> T5
    T3 --> T6

    style T5 fill:#FAEEDA,stroke:#BA7517,color:#412402
```

*(The amber "Action plans" subgraph marks the only screen with no backend calls — a product extension.)*

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `api/openapi.yaml` | API contract of the 23 endpoints — the source of truth |
| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |
| `export-screen-states.md` | Mapping between the export screen states and the export job statuses (RF05) |
| `sync-badge.md` | Semantics of the per-entry synchronization badge |
| `known-bugs.md` | Known non-blocking backend defects, with workarounds |
| `fixtures/` | Test media (audio, images for OCR), the expected transcription of the audio, and the three seeded entries used by semantic search |

Credentials (project URL and keys) are not in this package: they are provided in the app's `.env`.

## Contract path → function

`api/openapi.yaml` has no router: each operation is served by its own Edge Function at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` (see `servers` and each operation's `x-cerne-function` in the YAML) — **never** directly at the REST path below. Path parameters are appended as the final URL segments, in the same order as they appear in the path; any literal segment after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in the real URL.

| Contract path | Function (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>`) |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | `auth-signup` |
| `POST /auth/login` | `auth-login` |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | `auth-refresh` |
| `GET /auth/session` | `auth-session` |
| `POST /auth/logout` | `auth-logout` |
| `POST /entries` | `entries-create` |
| `GET /entries` | `entries-list` |
| `GET /entries/{id}` | `entries-get` |
| `GET /entries/search` | `entries-search` |
| `POST /media/ocr` | `media-ocr` |
| `POST /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-create` |
| `GET /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-list` |
| `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-list` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-send` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry` | `chat-messages-retry` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight` | `chat-insight-create` |
| `POST /export/summary` | `export-summary-create` |
| `GET /export/{jobId}/status` | `export-status-get` |
| `GET /export/{jobId}/download` | `export-download-get` |
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate` | `dashboard-aggregate-get` |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative` | `dashboard-narrative-get` |
| `PATCH /account/settings` | `account-settings-update` |
| `DELETE /account` | `account-delete` |

# Synchronization badge semantics

There is no `sync_status` column in the database: the architecture is cloud-only, so "it is on the server" already means "synchronized", by definition. The server neither stores nor computes a synchronization state; it only exposes two fields, and the **badge is derived entirely in the app** from them:

| Field | Where it appears in the contract | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `updatedAt` | `Entry.updatedAt` | Timestamp of the last server write for that entry. |
| `serverRevision` | `Entry.serverRevision`, and also in the profile | Counter that increases with every write to the user's entries — never resets, never decreases. |

**The badge's 3 states, all inferred on the client — none comes ready from the server:**
1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.

When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

First thing to flag: the brainstorm's open question about the local cache ("is drift's SQL overkill for RF06's AND-logic filters?") is built on a premise that doesn't hold up against the contract. I checked — `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` AND-filtering happens entirely server-side, as query params on `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` (openapi.yaml:500-520, 785-805). The client never runs that filter logic itself. So the real question isn't "can Hive do AND-logic" — it's "what does the local cache need to do at all, if it never filters anything?"

Second, sharper finding: `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md` explicitly contradicts the data-model table in requirements.md §8. Requirements.md lists a `sync_status` column on `entries`; the backend doc says flatly **there is no `sync_status` column** — the badge is derived entirely client-side from two fields the contract actually returns, `updatedAt` and `serverRevision` (confirmed in the Entry schema, openapi.yaml:600-614). Requirements.md itself says the contract wins on conflicts, so this is settled, but it means F000's `Entry` domain model needs `serverRevision`/`updatedAt`, not a `sync_status` enum pulled from the server.

**Winston:** Given that, the cache's job shrinks a lot. Looking at what actually needs offline access — RF07 timeline (view cached entries), and per backend README §6.3, `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` ("works offline (cache)") — every one of those is: store the last server response, keyed by id, replay it, dedupe on reconnect. No joins, no local predicate queries, because the server already owns every filter and every search. My working position: that kills the actual case for drift. A flat key-value store (Hive — two boxes, `entries` by id and `chat_messages` by session id, plus a cursor string for pagination) covers 100% of the stated offline need with less machinery than a relational engine nothing queries relationally.

**Priya:** Before I build RF06 on top of whatever you pick — convince me there's no case where I'll *wish* I had SQL. What about the My Records screen (Screen 4) combining a local list with a locally-applied secondary sort, or RF09's dashboard needing an aggregate over cached entries when `GET /dashboard/aggregate` itself fails? If any screen ever computes something *over* the cached set rather than just replaying it, Hive leaves you hand-rolling that in Dart instead of a query.

Do either of those land, or does Hive hold? And is there a scenario I'm not naming that would force relational structure back in?

# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.

`export_jobs` has two **independent** statuses — the status of the job itself (`status`) and the status of the AI-generated narrative (`narrativeStatus`) — because the raw export data can be ready before, after or independently of the narrative, and the UI must never block the download because of a narrative that failed. Circular. Keep flutter_secure_storage (plain, non-biometric-gated item) for the PIN hash + local_auth for Face ID/Touch ID, both owned by one vault state machine."

append lock "DI: plain get_it, no injectable/codegen. Each feature registers its own deps in a per-feature registration function called from main at startup."

append lock "DTOs/domain entities: freezed + json_serializable, justified concretely -- Entry alone has 11 required fields per the openapi.yaml schema (id, content, source, chatMessageId, occurredAt, tags, piiStatus, piiSpans, embeddingStatus, mediaDurationSeconds, serverRevision, createdAt, updatedAt), hand-written == / copyWith for that is a bug magnet. Also used for sealed unions (Failure, Resource). Not blanket codegen on every class."

append lock "Routing: go_router, single redirect callback keyed off one SessionStatus stream. No screen independently checks auth state or opts out of the gate."

append lock "HTTP client: dio + exactly one interceptor owning apikey/Authorization headers per AGENTS.md's header rule. Retry logic fires only for server retryable:true codes (NETWORK_TIMEOUT, NETWORK_OFFLINE, PII_CHECK_FAILED, EMBEDDING_FAILED, AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMITED) -- never for the 7 retryable:false codes (AUTH_EXPIRED, AUTH_INVALID, VALIDATION_ERROR, NOT_FOUND, EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, OCR_NO_TEXT)."

append lock "Failure hierarchy: sealed class with exactly 13 server-mirrored subtypes (full closed list from error-taxonomy.md: AuthExpired, AuthInvalid, NetworkTimeout, NetworkOffline, Validation, PiiCheckFailed, EmbeddingFailed, AiGenerationTimeout, NotFound, RateLimited, ExportEmptyPeriod, PayloadTooLarge, OcrNoText) plus exactly 1 local-only variant, MalformedResponse (retryable hardcoded false), for the 'malformed response' leg of RNF09's 3-failure-type test matrix -- that leg is NOT one of the 13 server codes, it is the client detecting a response that does not parse to the expected DTO shape. requirements.md section 11 lists only 10 of the 13 as 'minimum codes' -- the hierarchy must cover all 13, not just the 10 shown there."

append decision "RNF09 test harness: mocktail-stubs a single ApiClient interface (thin dio wrapper) per repository test, not a fake network transport/adapter layer. One shared table-driven test helper drives the 5-write-endpoints x 3-failure-types = 15 scenario matrix so later units fill a table instead of writing 15 tests from scratch."

append kill "Downgraded the brainstorm's 'one generic view-state enum shared by all nine screens' claim -- too strong. RF02's capture pipeline (recording/processing/transcribed/transcription-error) is its own state machine, not a data-fetch resource. RF07 depends on three independent streams at once (auth, sync badge, entry data) per its own acceptance criteria, not one Resource. Forcing either into a generic loading/error/data shape would be the wrong abstraction."

append lock "Shared view-state: a generic Resource<T> (idle/loading/data/error) in core, used only by single-source-of-truth fetch screens (e.g. RF06 results list, RF09 dashboard). RF02's capture state machine and RF07's composite auth x sync x data state get their own feature-specific state classes -- not forced into Resource<T>."

append decision "isolatedSideEffect helper (shared by RF08 and RF10's identical failure-isolation wording): the contract is decided now -- a never-throws wrapper returning Either<Failure,T> for an action that must not block its caller on failure -- but the implementation is deferred to RF10, its first real consumer in delivery order (RF04 -> RF10 -> RF08), not built speculatively in F000. It must live in core/ so RF08 can reuse it without a cross-feature import."

append lock "Chart package: fl_chart, unchanged from the brainstorm -- pure Dart, no native bridge, matches the 3 fixed RF09 scenarios (0/1/>30 entries)."

append lock "Entry domain model carries serverRevision (int) and updatedAt (timestamp) fields, not sync_status -- requirements.md section 8's data model table is wrong on this field; sync-badge.md and the Entry schema in openapi.yaml both confirm no such column exists. The 3-state sync badge (Synchronizing/Error/Synchronized) is a pure function computed client-side from serverRevision/updatedAt plus pending local-write state, never supplied by the server."

append note "AUTH_INVALID's description ('invalid credentials / biometrics') in requirements.md section 11 is imprecise: per the backend README, no biometric call ever reaches the server, so AUTH_INVALID can only ever originate from POST /auth/login (email+password). The vault's biometric/PIN gate stays 100% local with zero Either/Failure plumbing, consistent with the brainstorm's existing bedrock fact on this."

# F000 foundation — forged decisions

Source: 2026-10-25 brainstorm (`_bmad-output/brainstorming/brainstorm-f000-foundation-choices-2026-10-25/`) hardened against `docs/input/requirements.md`, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, and the rest of `docs/input/backend/`.

## Free-choice decisions

- **Local cache: Hive.** Not drift. Confirmed every filter/search dimension (`source`, `dateFrom`, `dateTo`, semantic search) is a server-side query param — the client never filters, joins or sorts cached data. Two boxes (`entries` by id, `chat_messages` by session id) + `chat_sessions` by id + a cursor string. Rejected: local secondary sort on My Records, client-side dashboard fallback aggregation — neither is a stated requirement.
- **Vault: flutter_secure_storage (plain PIN-hash item) + local_auth.** Rejected `biometric_storage` — gating storage behind biometric success can't satisfy RF03's "biometric failure falls back to PIN without lockout" (checking the PIN would need the hash, which would need biometric success, which is what just failed). Both paths owned by one vault state machine.
- **DI: plain get_it.** No injectable/codegen. Per-feature registration function, called from main.
- **DTOs/entities: freezed + json_serializable.** Justified by field count, not blanket codegen — Entry has 11 required fields in the contract; hand-written `==`/`copyWith` for that is a bug magnet. Also used for sealed unions (Failure, Resource).
- **Routing: go_router.** Single `redirect` callback keyed off one `SessionStatus` stream. No screen independently checks auth or opts out.
- **HTTP client: dio + one interceptor.** Owns apikey/Authorization headers. Retries only on server `retryable:true` codes (NETWORK_TIMEOUT, NETWORK_OFFLINE, PII_CHECK_FAILED, EMBEDDING_FAILED, AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT, RATE_LIMITED) — never the 7 `retryable:false` codes.
- **Chart: fl_chart.** Unchanged from the brainstorm — pure Dart, matches the 3 fixed RF09 scenarios.

## Shared abstractions (the real F000 deliverable)

- **Failure hierarchy:** sealed class, exactly 13 server-mirrored subtypes (full closed list — AuthExpired, AuthInvalid, NetworkTimeout, NetworkOffline, Validation, PiiCheckFailed, EmbeddingFailed, AiGenerationTimeout, NotFound, RateLimited, ExportEmptyPeriod, PayloadTooLarge, OcrNoText) + exactly 1 local-only variant, `MalformedResponse` (retryable hardcoded false), for RNF09's "malformed response" test leg — that leg isn't one of the 13 codes, it's the client's own parse-failure detection. requirements.md §11 shows only 10 of the 13 as "minimum" — the hierarchy covers all 13.
- **RNF09 test harness:** mocktail stubs a single `ApiClient` interface (thin dio wrapper) per repository test — not a fake transport/adapter layer. One shared table-driven helper drives the 5 endpoints × 3 failure-types = 15 scenario matrix.
- **View-state:** generic `Resource<T>` (idle/loading/data/error) in core, but only for single-source-of-truth fetch screens (RF06 results, RF09 dashboard). Rejected forcing it onto RF02 (capture pipeline: recording/processing/transcribed/error is its own state machine) or RF07 (composite of auth × sync × data, three independent streams) — downgraded the brainstorm's "one enum for all nine screens" claim as the wrong abstraction for those two.
- **isolatedSideEffect helper** (RF08/RF10 shared failure-isolation wording): contract decided now — never-throws wrapper returning `Either<Failure,T>` — but implementation deferred to RF10, its first real consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. Must live in `core/` so RF08 reuses it without a cross-feature import.
- **Entry domain model:** carries `serverRevision` (int) + `updatedAt` (timestamp), **not** `sync_status`. requirements.md §8's data-model table is wrong on this field — confirmed against `sync-badge.md` and the Entry schema in openapi.yaml. The 3-state sync badge is a pure function of these two fields plus pending-local-write state, computed client-side, never supplied by the server.

## Corrections to prior material

- requirements.md §8 (`entries.sync_status` column) contradicts `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`; the backend docs win per requirements.md's own precedence rule.
- requirements.md §11's error table is a 10-of-13 excerpt, not the full taxonomy; `error-taxonomy.md` is the complete closed list and must be what the Failure hierarchy is built from.
- AUTH_INVALID's "invalid credentials / biometrics" wording (§11) is imprecise — no biometric call ever reaches the server, so it can only originate from `POST /auth/login`.

## Open / explicitly deferred (not F000's job)

- isolatedSideEffect's concrete implementation — ships with RF10.
- Dashboard cache-invalidation behavior (RF09 AC) — a presentation-layer concern for whichever unit builds RF09, not a local-cache architecture decision.

- requirements.md §8 (`entries.sync_status` column) contradicts `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`; the backend docs win per requirements.md's own precedence rule.

- AUTH_INVALID's "invalid credentials / biometrics" wording (§11) is imprecise — no biometric call ever reaches the server, so it can only originate from `POST /auth/login`.

## Open / explicitly deferred (not F000's job)

- isolatedSideEffect's concrete implementation — ships with RF10.
- Dashboard cache-invalidation behavior (RF09 AC) — a presentation-layer concern for whichever unit builds RF09, not a local-cache architecture decision.
